scenes.name: the gap is one division
scenes.visual: Dark canvas, three horizontal bands, nothing clears. Top band (y 90–300): the puzzle bar from the thirty-millisecond chapter, at full size and laid out as the cold open drew it: a coral bar from x=210 to x=1710, y 160–220 (1,500 px = 30 ms, 50 px per millisecond), with a 5 px amber sliver at its left end and a thin white dimension line under it at y 242, spanning the bar. Its two text labels show only during b1: '30 ms per token', centred under the dimension line at (960, 278), and '0.1 ms arithmetic', left-anchored at (196, 118) above the sliver and joined to the sliver's top by a short amber leader, so the two never meet. After b1 the bar keeps its dimension line, without text, and a grey tag '× 300', left-anchored just right of the bar's right end at (1735, 198). Centre band (y 330–600): an equation that builds term by term: a fraction, amber 'peak' over coral 'bandwidth', then a white '÷', then a white chip '1 op per byte' with a tiny blue token pill on it, then '= ?'. Bottom band (y 680–960): two result rows that fill the equation in with numbers, one per chip, each led by a small GPU package icon and its name. Once both rows are written, the equation's word terms fade and its signs stay as a faint skeleton, so the coloured numbers below carry the meaning. At most five word labels on screen at any moment; the rest are numbers. Colour by meaning: amber arithmetic, coral memory, white results, grey caveats. The idea the motion makes visible: the puzzle's gap is one division, the chip's ridge over the workload's one operation per byte, and its exact size depends on which chip you divide for.

beats.say: Thirty milliseconds a token, and a tenth of one for its arithmetic. That gap is not a mystery. It is a division.
beats.show: On 'thirty milliseconds', the coral bar sweeps from x=210 to x=1710, the dimension line draws beneath it, and '30 ms per token' writes on centred under the line at (960, 278). On 'a tenth of one', the 5 px amber sliver lights at the bar's left end and '0.1 ms arithmetic' writes on above it at (196, 118), joined to the sliver's top by a short amber leader. On 'that gap', a grey bracket draws above the coral part at y 144, from x 240 to x 1710, and the tag '× 300' clicks on just right of the bar's right end. On 'a division', both text labels and the bracket fade out, leaving the bar, its dimension line, the sliver and the '× 300' tag, and a white '÷' fades in at centre stage, waiting for its terms.

beats.say: Two hardware numbers, peak arithmetic over bandwidth, make the chip's ridge. Divide by one property of the workload, decode's one operation per byte, and that is the gap.
beats.show: The equation builds centre stage. On 'peak arithmetic', amber 'peak' writes on left of the '÷'; on 'bandwidth', coral 'bandwidth' writes on beneath it with a fraction line; on 'the chip's ridge', a grey bracket under the fraction, label 'ridge'. On 'one property of the workload', the white chip '1 op per byte' slides in right of the '÷', with a grey bracket label 'decode'. On 'that is the gap', '= ?' writes on and a thin white line draws from the '?' up to the '× 300' tag on the bar, which pulses once.

beats.say: Two hundred and ninety-five on an H one hundred. On the H two hundred behind the thirty milliseconds, same arithmetic speed, faster memory, just over two hundred. Three hundred came from round numbers.
beats.show: The bracket labels 'ridge' and 'decode' fade. On 'two hundred and ninety-five', the first row writes on in the bottom band: GPU icon 'H100', amber '989' ÷ coral '3.35' ÷ white '1' = white '295', the result counting up, and the white line from '?' re-routes to it. On 'H two hundred', the second row writes on beneath: GPU icon 'H200', amber '989' ÷ coral '4.8' ÷ white '1' =, with a small stopwatch '29.2 ms' at its right end. On 'same arithmetic speed', both amber '989's pulse together. On 'faster memory', the coral '4.8' pulses, and the equation's word terms 'peak', 'bandwidth' and '1 op per byte' fade out, leaving its signs as a faint skeleton above the two coloured rows. On 'just over two hundred', the H200 result counts up to '206'. Then the top bar corrects itself at full size, one step per phrase, each step done within 0.4 s. On 'Three hundred', the '× 300' tag strikes through. On 'came from', the amber sliver widens from 5 to 7 px under a grey tag '0.1 ms was 0.14', in the old label's place with the same leader, while the coral bar and its dimension line trim back from x=1710 to x=1668 and a grey tag '30 ms was 29.2' writes on centred under the line at (939, 278). On 'round numbers', the struck tag slides left with the bar's end and rolls to '× 206', tied by a white line to the H200 row's '206'. The corrected bar then holds, still, through the rest of the line and the scene's 1 s tail, about 1.5 s, before the cut. Word labels left at the end: 'H100', 'H200', '0.1 ms was 0.14', '30 ms was 29.2'.

scenes.name: the chain, in five links
scenes.visual: New composition. Top-left, a small grey heading 'The chain, in five links', 28 px, left-anchored at (120, 128), clear of the chapter kicker; it fades on 'a forward pass'. Across the frame (x 120–1500): five link cards stacked vertically, each 128 px tall with 40 px gaps (y 160–960), blue outlines. Inside each card, left to right: a numbered circle '1' to '5' centred at x 172, a small icon (x 220–330), the card's title in white, 30 px, left-anchored at x 360 and ending before x 920, and at the right end (x 950–1480) its result chip, 26 px mono, which carries its own operation so the ÷ or × sign is visible. The five titles, exactly: 1 'compute outgrows bandwidth'; 2 'a forward pass streams every weight'; 3 'prefill amortises, decode does not'; 4 'the KV cache adds to the bill'; 5 'goodput is what is actually sold'. In each gap a chain-link icon (two interlocking rings), under the numbered circles, joins a card to the next. Right of the stack (x 1560–1800): a large stopwatch centred at (1680, 520) reading '30 ms', joined to the whole stack by one tall white bracket at x 1525 running from the top of card 1 to the bottom of card 5, its point toward the stopwatch. The card being spoken about is at full brightness; finished cards dim to 60%. Card icons and chips: 1, two vertical arrows drawn to scale, amber 120 px and coral 26 px (80 : 17), chip '80 ÷ 17 ≈ 4.7'; 2, a GPU package with a coral stream on its bus, chip coral '70 bn × 2 bytes = 140 GB'; 3, one coral read stream fanning into a block of blue pills above a second stream feeding one lone pill, chip coral '140 GB ÷ 4.8 TB/s = 29.2 ms' (about 460 px, the widest one-line chip); 4, a short stack of coral K V slabs, each split into a 'K' half and a 'V' half, matching the K V cache drawings earlier in the film, chip coral on two lines, '2 × 80 × 8 × 128 × 2 B' over '≈ 320 KB'; 5, the goodput gate from the previous chapter in miniature, a narrow doorway on a short pipe with a stopwatch icon above it and a small grey bin below, chip teal 'throughput × share on time'. The idea the motion makes visible: five short statements, each carrying one piece of arithmetic, chained into a single explanation of the thirty milliseconds.

beats.say: Five sentences explain the thirty milliseconds. Compute outgrows bandwidth, eighty times against seventeen in a decade, so the ridge climbs. A forward pass streams every weight, a hundred and forty gigabytes a token.
beats.show: On 'five sentences', the heading writes on and the five empty cards fade in, their numbered circles and chain links drawing top to bottom. On 'the thirty milliseconds', the stopwatch '30 ms' appears at right and its bracket draws down the whole stack. On 'compute outgrows bandwidth', card 1's title writes on, 'compute outgrows bandwidth'; on 'eighty times', its amber arrow grows to full height; on 'seventeen', its coral arrow grows to about a fifth of that; on 'the ridge climbs', chip 1 writes on, '80 ÷ 17 ≈ 4.7'. On 'a forward pass', card 1 dims, the heading fades and card 2's title writes on, 'a forward pass streams every weight'; on 'every weight', a coral stream runs across its GPU icon's bus; on 'a hundred and forty gigabytes', chip 2 writes on, '70 bn × 2 bytes = 140 GB'.

beats.say: Prefill amortises that read, decode does not: every token pays it in full. The K V cache adds to the bill, three hundred and twenty kilobytes per token held.
beats.show: Card 2 dims. On 'prefill amortises', card 3's title writes on, 'prefill amortises, decode does not', and its upper stream fans out into the block of blue pills, all lighting at once; on 'decode does not', the lower stream, just as wide, feeds its one lone pill; on 'pays it in full', chip 3 writes on, '140 GB ÷ 4.8 TB/s = 29.2 ms', and the stopwatch at right ticks once. On 'the K V cache', card 3 dims and card 4's title writes on, 'the KV cache adds to the bill', its stack of coral K V slabs growing by one; on 'three hundred and twenty kilobytes', chip 4 builds term by term on its first line, '2 × 80 × 8 × 128 × 2 B', then '≈ 320 KB' writes on beneath it.

beats.say: And goodput, the tokens that arrive in time, is what is actually sold. Each link is a division or a multiplication you can now do yourself, nothing beyond arithmetic.
beats.show: On 'goodput', card 4 dims and card 5's title writes on, 'goodput is what is actually sold'; small blue tokens run along its pipe to the gate, those in time passing through and turning teal, late ones turning grey and dropping into the bin. On 'actually sold', chip 5 writes on in teal, 'throughput × share on time'. On 'a division or a multiplication', all five cards return to full brightness, the camera eases back about 5% so the chain and the stopwatch sit centred with a margin round them, and the signs in the chips light amber one chip after another, top to bottom: the ÷ in chip 1, the × in chip 2, the ÷ in chip 3, the four × in chip 4, the × in chip 5. On 'nothing beyond arithmetic', the bracket from the chain to the stopwatch glows white along its full length and holds.

scenes.name: the road ahead
scenes.visual: New composition. Top band: one division, large and centred on a single line, term boxes 56 px tall (y 102–158) with 34 px type, clear of the chapter kicker. It builds term by term: white 'tokens per second' right-aligned to x 500, white '=' at x 528, a coral box 'bandwidth' (x 560–760), white '÷' at x 822, and a coral box 'bytes per token' starting at x 885. On cue, 'bytes per token' splits into a bracketed pair: white '(' at x 862, coral box 'bytes per read' (x 885–1175), white '÷' at x 1238, blue box 'tokens sharing each read' (x 1265–1730), white ')' at x 1790. The brackets are essential: the line must read tokens per second = bandwidth ÷ (bytes per read ÷ tokens sharing each read), the split staying inside the denominator, so more tokens per read means more tokens per second (ten sharing: 3.35 TB/s ÷ (140 GB ÷ 10) ≈ 239 a second; without brackets it would wrongly read as 2.4). Each of the three final terms carries a small teal arrow, 28 px, just right of its box (at x 768, 1183 and 1738), and owns a port, a small dot coloured like the term, on the panel's top edge directly below the term's centre: port A x 660 under 'bandwidth', port B x 1030 under 'bytes per read', port C x 1498 under 'tokens sharing each read', all at y 330. When a term's first card wires up, a vertical line in the term's colour draws from the term's box straight down to its port. Annotation row (y 186–270), between the equation and the panel: it holds one chip at a time, 24 px mono, centred under its term and threaded on that term's port line like a tag on a wire, and each chip leads with the 24 tokens a second baseline: A 'H100 24 → H200 ≈ 34 tokens/s' (x 440–880); B '16-bit 24 → 8-bit ≈ 48 tokens/s' (x 790–1270); C '1 user 24 → 10 users ≈ 240 in all' (x 1242–1754), with a smaller grey second line inside the same chip, 'weights only'. A chip fades as the next card is named, and the row is empty by b4. Lower part: a large rounded blue panel, x 120–1800, y 330–1010. Its title 'Where the series goes from here' sits inside its top-left corner at (168, 372) during b1 only, and fades before any wire is drawn. Eight cards, 360 × 200 px, in a 4 × 2 grid with 48 px gutters: columns x 168–528, 576–936, 984–1344, 1392–1752; row one y 420–620, row two y 680–880. Each card has an icon, a tiny grey video number in its top-left corner and a label, exactly as listed. Row one: '2' 'inside the GPU' (a chip icon), '3' 'the code on it' (a code-brackets icon), '4' 'fewer bits' (a row of sixteen binary digits), '5' 'across many chips' (two chip icons joined by a link). Row two: '6' 'part of itself' (a pie with one slice lit), '7' 'serving at scale' (a crowd of user icons), '8' 'idle units in decode' (a sleeping chip with a small 'z'), '9' 'one real request' (a route icon). Cards start dimmed to 30%, showing only icon and number. As each is named it brightens to full, its label writes on and its wire draws to its port; when the next card is named, the previous label fades, leaving icon, number and wire, so at most one card label is on screen. Wire routing: every wire runs in vertical and horizontal segments only and never crosses a card. It leaves its card's top-edge centre. A row-one wire goes straight up. A row-two wire goes up to y 650, the gap between the rows, then sideways to the gutter on its left (x 144 for column 1, then x 552, 960 and 1368), then up that gutter. Every wire then joins its term's rail just inside the panel's top edge (rail A y 360, rail B y 378, rail C y 396), runs along it to its port's x and rises into the port. Wires take their term's colour: coral to 'bandwidth' and to 'bytes per read', blue to 'tokens sharing each read'. Cards 2 to 8 send one wire each and card 9 sends three, one to each port: ten wires in all. The panel's bottom strip (y 950) is kept free for card 9's miniature route. The idea the motion makes visible: eight later videos, one division, each pulling on one of its terms.

beats.say: For decode, flip the thirty-millisecond division: tokens per second is bandwidth over bytes per token. Bytes per token is bytes per read over the tokens sharing it. Those three terms are the escape routes from earlier.
beats.show: On 'For decode', a grey line '140 GB ÷ 4.8 TB/s = 29.2 ms' fades in at the centre of the top band; on 'flip the thirty-millisecond division', it flips in place to '4.8 TB/s ÷ 140 GB ≈ 34 tokens/s'. On 'tokens per second', the grey line dissolves and the division writes on in its place, term by term: 'tokens per second', '=', coral 'bandwidth', '÷', coral 'bytes per token'. On 'bytes per read', the 'bytes per token' box splits: it narrows to coral 'bytes per read', a white '÷' and a blue box 'tokens sharing each read' slide out to its right, and white brackets close round the pair. On 'tokens sharing it', the blue box glows once. On 'three terms', a small teal arrow appears beside each term in turn: up beside 'bandwidth', down beside 'bytes per read', up beside 'tokens sharing each read'. On 'from earlier', the panel fades in below with its title and eight dimmed cards, icons and numbers only; the title fades at the end of the beat.

beats.say: Ahead: inside the G P U, and the code on it. Fewer bits per weight. One model across many chips.
beats.show: On 'inside the G P U', card 2 brightens, its label 'inside the GPU' writes on, and its coral wire draws up to rail A and along to port A; the port line rises into 'bandwidth', and chip A appears in the annotation row, threaded on that line: 'H100 24 → H200 ≈ 34 tokens/s'. On 'the code on it', card 2's label fades; card 3 brightens with its label and wires coral along rail B to port B, whose line rises into 'bytes per read', and that term's teal arrow pulses. On 'fewer bits', card 3's label fades; card 4 brightens with its label, its sixteen binary digits shrink to eight, and it wires coral to port B; chip A fades as chip B appears under 'bytes per read': '16-bit 24 → 8-bit ≈ 48 tokens/s'. On 'many chips', card 4's label fades; card 5 brightens with its label and wires coral along rail A to port A, and the arrow beside 'bandwidth' pulses.

beats.say: Models using only part of themselves per token. Serving at scale. Decode's idle arithmetic, put to work. And one real request, traced end to end through the whole stack.
beats.show: On 'part of themselves', card 5's label and chip B fade; card 6 brightens with its label, and its coral wire runs up the left-margin gutter and along rail B to port B. On 'serving at scale', card 6's label fades; card 7 brightens with its label and draws a blue wire up its gutter and along rail C to port C, whose line rises into 'tokens sharing each read'; chip C appears under that term, '1 user 24 → 10 users ≈ 240 in all', with 'weights only' in small grey type on the chip's second line. On 'idle arithmetic', card 7's label and chip C fade; card 8's sleeping chip wakes, its label writes on with a small amber tag beneath it, '> 99% idle at batch 1', and it wires blue to port C. On 'one real request', card 8's label and tag fade; card 9 brightens with its label, and three wires leave it at once up its gutter, one along each rail, to ports A, B and C. On 'end to end', the six-stop route from earlier draws in miniature along the panel's bottom strip at y 950, from x 200 to x 1720: six small icon dots, the signpost, queue, document, hand-off arrows, loop and laptop icons of that route, joined by a line, with one blue token pill travelling along it. On 'the whole stack', the pill reaches the laptop and the whole route glows once.

beats.say: Each attacks that division, most by moving one term. Hold that frame, and the series reads as a single argument.
beats.show: All eight cards are at full brightness, icons and numbers only, each wired to its term; the annotation row is empty and card 9's route has faded, so the equation's four text items are the only words on screen. On 'that division', the division pulses once and all ten wires pulse with it, a light running up each wire, through its port, into its term. On 'most by', card 9's three wires pulse once more, together, while every other card's single wire holds. On 'moving one term', each term's teal arrow nudges once in its own direction. On 'a single argument', all ten wires and the three port lines glow white together, so the whole grid reads as one network feeding the division, and the panel dims to 50% so the division and its wiring hold the frame.

scenes.name: closing
scenes.visual: Everything clears to the dark canvas: a quiet, spacious ending. Centre, a single blue token pill beside a stopwatch, a callback to the film's first picture of tokens streaming out. Then two short lines in two colours. Then the end card: the film's title, the series name and what comes next. Slow, unhurried motion; long holds.

beats.say: Arithmetic is cheap. Data movement is expensive.
beats.show: From the clear canvas, a blue token pill settles at centre beside a stopwatch reading '30 ms'; a thin coral stream flows beneath it, left to right, and a tiny amber dot beside the stream blinks once and sits still. On 'arithmetic is cheap', amber 'Arithmetic is cheap.' writes on above the pill; on 'data movement is expensive', coral 'Data movement is expensive.' writes on beneath it. Hold two seconds.

beats.say: Next, inside the G P U. This has been The Memory Wall.
beats.show: The pill, stream and two lines rise and fade. On 'inside the G P U', a small blue card with a chip icon fades in near the bottom: 'Next: Inside the GPU'. On 'The Memory Wall', the title 'The Memory Wall' fades in at centre in large white type, with 'The Engineering Behind LLM Inference · video 1 of 9' beneath it in grey. Hold three seconds after the last word, then fade to black.

checks.claim: Puzzle (as stated in the cold open and ch05): 10^11 ops / 10^15 ops/s = 0.1 ms of arithmetic
Puzzle factor: 30 ms / 0.1 ms = 300 (round numbers)
Puzzle bar: 0.1 ms sliver on a 1,500 px bar for 30 ms is 5 px
Tag '0.1 ms was 0.14': unrounded arithmetic per token = 140e9 / 989e12 = 0.14 ms
Tag '30 ms was 29.2', stopwatch '29.2 ms' and the s03 grey line '140 GB ÷ 4.8 TB/s = 29.2 ms': 140 GB / 4.8 TB/s = 29.2 ms
Corrected bar: 0.1416 ms sliver = 7 px; 29.17 ms bar = 1,458 px, so its right end and dimension line trim from x=1710 to x=1668, and the tag '30 ms was 29.2' centres under the trimmed line at x 939
Decode intensity: (2 x 70 billion ops) / (70 billion x 2 bytes) = 1 op per byte
Ridge on H100: 989 TFLOP/s / 3.35 TB/s = 295 ops per byte
Ridge on H200: same 989 TFLOP/s dense 16-bit (same compute die; a hardware fact also used in ch17, not stated in the atlas) / 4.8 TB/s = 206 ops per byte
Gap on H100 = memory time / arithmetic time = (140e9/3.35e12) / (140e9/989e12) = 295 = ridge / 1

REVIEWER BLOCKER FIX: gap on the H200 that produced the 30 ms = (140e9/4.8e12) / (140e9/989e12) = 206.04, not 295 and not 300; the puzzle's 300 came from rounding (0.14 ms down to 0.1, 29.2 ms up to 30). ch05 already said 'about two hundred times rather than three' unrounded.
Gap = ridge / decode intensity = (peak / bandwidth) / (ops per byte), for both chips

CORRECTION to fig 146 label 'the factor of 300 = bandwidth / bytes per token': bandwidth / bytes per token is a rate, 23.9 tokens/s on an H100 (the decode ceiling), not a dimensionless factor. The film states the gap as (peak / bandwidth) / (ops per byte) = ridge / intensity: 295 on an H100, 206 on an H200, i.e. two hardware numbers and one property of the workload, as the figure's prose says.
Link 1: compute x80 vs bandwidth x17 over a decade = 4.7x, so the ridge climbs about fivefold (ch06's figures)
Link 1 icon: arrows to scale, amber 120 px vs coral 120 x 17/80 = 25.5 px (about a fifth)
Link 2: 70 billion weights x 2 bytes = 140 GB per token
Link 3: decode pays the full read every token: 140 GB / 4.8 TB/s = 29.2 ms on an H200
Link 4: KV cache per token 2 x 80 x 8 x 128 x 2 = 327,680 bytes, about 320 KB

Road ahead, slot A 'H100 24 → H200 ≈ 34 tokens/s' and the s03 grey line flipped to '4.8 TB/s ÷ 140 GB ≈ 34 tokens/s' (ch12's raise-bandwidth example): baseline 3.35 TB/s / 140 GB = 24, H200 4.8 TB/s / 140 GB = 34 tokens/s
Road ahead, slot B '16-bit 24 → 8-bit ≈ 48 tokens/s' (ch12): baseline 24; 8-bit weights halve 140 GB to 70 GB; 3.35 TB/s / 70 GB = about 48 tokens/s
Road ahead, slot C '1 user 24 → 10 users ≈ 240 in all', 'weights only' (ch12): 10 requests sharing one read of the weights = about 240 tokens/s in all, each user still about 24
Road ahead, card 8 tag '> 99% idle at batch 1': 1 - 1/ridge = 99.7% on an H100, 99.5% on an H200

REVIEWER MAJOR FIX, s03 equation: the screen must read bandwidth ÷ (bytes per read ÷ tokens sharing each read), i.e. bytes per token = bytes per read ÷ tokens sharing (ch10, ch12). With the brackets, ten users give 239 tokens/s, matching slot C; read left to right without them, the same terms would give 2.4, which is why the brackets are mandatory

H200 gap narrated as 'just over two hundred' (consistent with ch05's 'about two hundred times rather than three') and shown as '206', so it is not heard as a repeat of ch17's 'two hundred and six times less work' (Example A, 1032 / 5), an unrelated number
Layout: s02 stack of five 128 px cards with 40 px gaps spans 800 px, y 160–960; s03 grid of four 360 px columns with 48 px gutters spans 1,584 px, x 168–1752

s02 chip widths at 26 px mono (about 0.6 em per character, 40 px padding) against the 530 px chip zone x 950–1480: chip 3 about 461 px fits; chip 4 on one line about 524 px is too tight, so it builds on two lines, the longer about 383 px
s03 slot chips at 24 px mono (about 0.6 em per character, 36 px padding), centred under their terms at x 660, 1030 and 1498, stay inside the 1,920 px frame: A x 440–880, B x 789–1271, C x 1242–1754
s03 wires: cards 2 to 8 send one each, card 9 sends three, so 'all ten wires' in b4
